profile.summary: Abhinav Uppal uses game-theory models to understand how firms compete on price and when rivals are better off cooperating. His recent work looks at unusual alliances between competitors: online retailers that let customers return items at a rival's stores, and streaming services that make it easy to subscribe to each other. He is also interested in how traditional retailers can respond to e-commerce, and has written on the future of the marketing mix and on AI's effects on society.

themes.name: Alliances between competitors
themes.description: When partnerships between rivals, such as shared returns or streaming tie-ups, soften price competition, and who gains: the partners, outsiders or consumers.

themes.name: Platform pricing and regulation
themes.description: Two-sided models of internet pricing that ask how content business models change the stakes of network neutrality.

themes.name: Marketing's changing landscape
themes.description: How technology, AI, regulation and geopolitics are reshaping marketing decisions, and why human oversight of AI matters.
